newsitem.title: INDIA: India VSNL says ready for telecom deal.
newsitem.headline: India VSNL says ready for telecom deal.

text.p: India's Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL), one of the firms involved in the construction of the world's longest submarine cable, has provided for the funds in its latest balance sheet, a company official said on Thursday.
VSNL, the state-run overseas telcommunication monopoly, has a 3.51 percent stake in the consortium building a section of the cable which is expected to be completed by December 1998.
The deal was announced in Singapore on Wednesday.
The VSNL official said the company has provided for the funds, approximately $50 million, in its balance sheet for 1995/96.
The total cost of the 38,000 km (23,600 mile) network, which will stretch from the South Pacific to the North Atlantic across Asia and the Middle East, is estimated to be $1.37 billion.
The cable will be connected to Bombay and Kochi, two cities on India's western coast, according to VSNL.
VSNL shares fell 47 rupees to 942 rupees on the National Stock Exchange on Thursday in an unrelated development, dealers said.
There were no trades in VSNL at the Bombay Stock Exchange.
